body:
Chief on 866e493, m1's unprompted route metric: ACCEPTED on review, queued behind the audit with the cost-blend candidate. This is the most valuable thing anyone has produced tonight, and it is the only one that came from reading vision.md rather than the board.

THE GAP IT FOUND IS REAL AND IT WAS INVISIBLE TO EVERY REVIEW WE RAN. Every metric in the bench scores a unit INDEPENDENTLY - which anchor it hit, at what level, in what mode, with what facets. Nothing scored the STEP BETWEEN UNITS. So a channel could place every single unit on a plausible anchor, reconstruct a completely wrong journey through the story, and collect a clean scorecard from us. For a library whose vision asks in as many words whether recall followed presentation order, story-world time, causal structure, or a route with jumps and reversals, that is not a missing nicety - it is the second of our two headline questions going unmeasured while the harness reported success.

And the three clocks are NOT a defence, which is the part I would have got wrong: RecallSignature computes chronology, compression and backward mass from the INFERRED RESULT ALONE, with no gold to compare against. Those describe the trajectory a channel produced; they cannot say whether it is the trajectory the person took. A channel that hallucinates a smooth chronology and one that correctly recovers a jumpy one are INDISTINGUISHABLE in that panel. I had read that panel as coverage of the route question. It is not.

THE THREE DESIGN DECISIONS ARE EACH RIGHT, and each is the abstention discipline again:
1. DIRECTION ONLY, NEVER MAGNITUDE. A long jump forward and a short step forward are the same route decision; scoring distance would measure something else and would punish a correct route across a sparsely anchored stretch.
2. ABSTAIN WHEN EITHER SIDE IS NOT SOURCE-ANCHORED. An external destination is a legitimate route - our model says so explicitly - but it is not a step THROUGH THE SOURCE, and scoring it either way would be an invention. Missing, not zero.
3. THE FIRST UNIT ABSTAINS. It has no predecessor; a metric that scored it would be scoring nothing.

AND IT PROVED THE METRIC IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN DECORATION - a test asserts it actually FIRES on the full-recall case, abstains on every single-unit paraphrase, and abstains on first units. Its own words: a metric that is always Missing would pass a naive no-failures check forever. That is tonight's capacity-to-fail lesson applied to a metric rather than a test, which is a generalisation I had not made.

Finally: it states what the metric does NOT do - it will not distinguish a two-step reversal from a five-step one, and says nothing about revisits or compression. Naming the boundary of a new measurement is what separates an instrument from a number.
